original_test_intent: Verify the specified Type-C hub converts the intended SUT display path to the approved VGA or HDMI monitor and produces a stable, readable image at the required mode without blanking, artifacts, flicker or system/display-path errors.
original_method: Select by row/variant; bind SUT Type-C receptacle through controller/mux/retimer/GPU or BMC display source to hub, adapter/cable and monitor EDID; inspect and connect under approved power/hot-plug procedure; show a known visual pattern; operator observes resolution/refresh, stability, color/orientation and artifacts while optional read-only DRM/BMC logs identify the path; preserve photos/video and disconnect/leave setup only as approved.
manual_activity: A qualified operator connects the exact hub/display chain and observes a known rendered pattern; the agent can only organize supplied artifacts and optional read-only diagnostics.
required_inputs: Unique identity resolution for the duplicate code
Exact SUT Type-C receptacle, controller/mux/retimer and GPU/BMC display-source route
Approved Type-C hub PN/firmware/power, VGA-or-HDMI output, cable/adapter and monitor PN/serial/EDID
Supported/required resolution, refresh, color/orientation, known pattern, stability/artifact rubric and connection procedure
safety_requirements: Select by row/variant and never execute same-code SEL reservation commands
Inspect connector/hub/cable power and compatibility before connection
Use only approved hot-plug or powered-down sequence and never force connectors
Do not accept logical enumeration as proof of visible pixels
Stop on resistance, abnormal heat, unstable link, blanking, artifacts, flicker or new display/system errors; no repeated reconnect
agent_execution_scope: Validate composite identity, display-path map, fixture and visual rubric
Label/hash operator photos/video and optional read-only EDID/connector/error evidence
Correlate artifacts and timestamps without claiming direct sight
Do not touch hardware, reserve SEL, change display settings, clear logs, reconnect/retry or decide verdict
engineer_actions: Resolve duplicate-code ownership while preserving both rows
Approve display source/path, hub/monitor fixture, mode and visual criteria
Review physical evidence and decide PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The described manual connection and observation match the Screen row; no SSH or SEL command can replace it.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Operator connects the approved Type-C-hub-to-VGA/HDMI monitor chain once, displays the known pattern and records mode, stability and image-quality observations with photos/video.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The Type-C hub, VGA/HDMI monitor, normal-display criterion and 5/5-minute estimates remain; an explicit oracle is added rather than inferred.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Bind the full physical/logical display chain and observe a known pattern at an approved mode, retaining physical and diagnostic evidence.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds collision-safe selection, display-source/path/fixture identity, mode/EDID, visual rubric, safe connection and stop criteria.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A connector status, EDID or row-1195 SEL reservation cannot prove that the physical monitor renders a normal image.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Hub conversion, cable and monitor can each cause failures; visual quality remains operator-owned and may require a standardized pattern to be repeatable.

project_override_considerations: Engineering must specify whether the source is host GPU, BMC/DPoC or another controller and whether both VGA and HDMI paths are required or one approved path is sufficient.
expected_evidence: Exact row/variant/hash and explicit separation from row 1195 SEL reservation
Approved connection procedure and before/connected/final photos
EDID and selected resolution/refresh/color/orientation where observable
Known-pattern photo/video plus operator blanking/flicker/artifact/readability result
Preserved display/BMC/kernel errors, damage/discrepancy record and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Wistron-BMC-00485-V003 identifies both row 1195 Reserve SEL (OOB) and row 2204 physical Screen. The row/variant resolves this review, but code-only selection could dispatch an unrelated stateful SEL operation.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The physical display objective is clear. Exact path, fixture, mode and visual rubric are supplyable prerequisites.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Functionality row 2204 Wistron-BMC-00485-V003: assign/approve a unique identity distinct from row 1195 Reserve SEL; approve the Type-C receptacle/controller/mux/retimer and GPU-versus-BMC display-source path, Type-C hub PN/firmware/power and VGA/HDMI output, cable/monitor/EDID fixture, required resolution/refresh/color/orientation, known-pattern stability/artifact rubric, hot-plug/power procedure, error limits and cleanup.

review_improvement: Prevents same-code SEL misdispatch and makes the manual screen result traceable to a defined display path, fixture, mode and visual oracle.
independent_technical_reasoning: The test set suggests BMC KVM/DPoC, but the physical Type-C-to-monitor route does not itself reveal whether pixels originate from BMC or host GPU. That source must be mapped to preserve intent. A visible desktop is also insufficient without the specified mode and stability/artifact observation. Because the identical code owns a SEL reservation elsewhere, composite identity is required before any action and the physical evidence can never be merged with repository-state evidence.
